heroHeadline: Sudan's Lean Season Emergency Begins — UN Projects 28.9M Acutely Hungry at Peak; UNSC Briefed as RSF Drone Campaign and Eid Massacres Remain Unaccountable
heroSubtitle: June 1, 2026 marks the onset of Sudan's June–August lean season — IPC's highest-risk window, projected to push acute hunger to 28.9 million people (half the population), with IPC Phase 5 famine confirmed in El Fasher and Kadugli and 20+ areas at critical risk. The lean season begins as Chad's Adre border crossing remains closed following the RSF's May 25 Al-Tina market strike (14 killed), and the UN Security Council convenes its June 2026 Sudan briefing with no ceasefire mechanism in place 38 months into the war. RSF drone attacks continued daily: a May 30 strike on the Abu Zabad–Al-Fula road (West Kordofan) killed 10 civilians; the Eid al-Adha massacres at Al-Murrah (27–60 killed, May 29) and Misterei (28–97 Masalit killed, May 28) remain unaccountable. SAF advances in Blue Nile continued on May 26 with five Qaysan district towns retaken, pushing RSF and SPLM-N toward Ethiopia. Khartoum's cholera outbreak (2,500 cases in three weeks) deepens as the rainy season cuts road access to isolated communities. 34 million Sudanese — 65% of the population — require urgent humanitarian support; the 2026 appeal is only 20% funded.
